title: Advanced JSONB & SQL/JSON Path Expressions
description: Query complex nested documents using jsonb_path_query, jsonb_set, and transform schemas dynamically.

data.text: PostgreSQL implements the SQL:2016 standard for **SQL/JSON path expressions** (`jsonb_path_query`, `jsonb_path_exists`). JSON Path allows traversing deep, polymorphic JSON trees using JavaScript-like dot notation and predicate filters.

data.title: Querying Nested JSON Arrays with JSON Path
data.content: Extracting items filtered by nested conditions.

data.text: `jsonb_set` replaces or creates a value at a specific path, and `||` merges two objects. Both return a new document, so they are used in an `UPDATE`. The `#>` and `#>>` operators navigate deep paths with an array of keys, which is convenient when the path itself is dynamic.

data.title: Update one key without rewriting the document
data.content: The first statement patches a nested key; the second merges new top-level keys. Neither replaces the whole document blindly.
data.code:
UPDATE events
SET payload = jsonb_set(payload, '{status}', '"processed"')
WHERE id = 42;

-- Merge extra metadata into the document
UPDATE events
SET payload = payload || '{"reviewed": true, "reviewer": "ada"}'::jsonb
WHERE id = 42;

-- Read a deep value with a dynamic path array
SELECT payload #>> '{customer,address,city}' AS city
FROM events
WHERE id = 42;

data.title: Normalize what you filter, store JSON for the rest
data.text: JSONB is excellent for fields that vary by row and are read as a whole — event payloads, settings, feature flags. It is a poor choice for columns you filter, join, or aggregate frequently, because every query has to extract the value and an index on it is awkward. A common pattern is to keep the stable, queried attributes as real columns and the flexible remainder in a JSONB column. Interviewers look for exactly that judgement.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: JSON Path (`jsonb_path_query`) provides standard path traversal syntax.
Use `jsonb_set` to mutate specific nested keys without replacing the whole document.
Combine JSON Path with GIN indexing for ultra-fast document search.
